newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir crew prepares for redocking of supply ship.
newsitem.headline: Mir crew prepares for redocking of supply ship.

text.p: The three-man crew aboard Russia's Mir space station on Sunday prepared to redock with a supply craft containing fuel supplies and garbage.

A spokesman at Mission Control just outside Moscow said preparations were going ahead "on plan" for the redocking of the Progress supply ship, which will take place at 5.54 p.m. Moscow time (1354 GMT).

The manoeuvre repeats a procedure carried out on June 25 when a different Progress vehicle docking with Mir collided with the station's Spektr module, causing a major loss of power in the worst accident of the space station's 11-year history.
On Sunday however, Mir will attempt the docking in automatic rather than manual pilot as happened in June.
The current Progress craft, which is seven metres (23 feet) long and weighs 7,200 kg (15,800 pounds), delivered oxygen, food, water and tools to Mir on July 7.
It undocked on August 6 to make room for a Soyuz spaceship bringing relief cosmonauts Anatoly Solovyov and Pavel Vinogradov to Mir.
Space officials said redocking a trash-filled module helps Mir by providing balance for the station and by protecting the hatch from prolonged solar exposure.
The crew will also draw on Progress' 200 kg (440 pound) supply of fuel before the supply ship is dumped into the Pacific Ocean in early October, they said.
Next Wednesday, commander Solovyov and flight engineer Vinogradov plan to put on spacesuits inside the Mir capsule -- a rare event in spaceflight -- and open the hatch to the darkened Spektr module.

They will then attempt to attach cables into the module, which will restore much power to Mir, and then reseal Spektr. They hope to patch the puncture in several external spacewalks starting in September.

On Friday, the three-man crew, which also includes British-born U.S. astronaut Michael Foale, circled Mir for 45 minutes in the Soyuz escape capsule filming and photographing the exterior of Spektr in preparation for the risky repair work.
